Reader guide

Questions this evidence can help you investigate.

Compare locations and property classes, understand the advertised stock competing for attention, and identify observations to validate further. Area benchmarks describe asking prices within broad classes; they do not value an individual property.

ReaderUseful starting pointWhat to verify next
Buyers and tenantsCity briefs and the area price bookActual property specification, availability, annual rent and additional charges
Estate surveyors and valuersDated area/class benchmarks and coverageBedrooms, floor area, condition, tenure and achieved comparable transactions
DevelopersProduct mix, concentration and competing advertised stockNew supply pipeline, permissions and actual absorption
Investors and fund managersExposure concentration and differences between segmentsMatched rental/sale evidence, vacancy and costs before modelling returns
Governments and researchersSpatial coverage and formal advertised-market observationsRepresentative household, population and housing-stock evidence

Read the measures consistently

“Active” is a weekly stock count. “New” means first discovered by the scraper, not necessarily newly built or newly marketed. “Reductions” counts events, not the percentage discount or completed deals. A neighbourhood with few advertisements is not automatically an underserved market.

The period at a glance.

02 / sales · Inventory

Sales Market Analysis

Through the PS-0 PropertyScraper lens, sales inventory observations cover 10 cities and 282 city/neighbourhood pairs. Lekki Phase 1 (LAGOS) maintained the highest concentration, averaging 726.8 active listings per observed week. This was followed by Lekki (LAGOS) with 702.5 average weekly active listings and Ikoyi (LAGOS) with 434.8 average weekly active listings.

sales / Asking prices

Compare asking-price benchmarks.

Advertised asking price benchmarks across property classes show class-specific scales. For Detached Houses, Central Business District (ABUJA) recorded a mean observed group median of ₦5.7M (5.0 average weekly active listings across 4 priced weeks), while Banana Island (LAGOS) reached ₦4.5B (64.8 average weekly active listings across 4 priced weeks). For 2 Bed Flats, Jakande (LAGOS) registered ₦24.0M (6.0 average weekly listings), whereas Victoria Island (LAGOS) stood at ₦452.5M (62.5 average weekly listings).

What this means for comparisons

Use city and class benchmarks before interpreting an aggregate asking price. A large supply of land in one city and flats in another can change the national mix without any comparable property becoming more expensive. New discoveries also reflect collection activity, and should not be treated as construction completions.

What to monitor next

Compare geographic and property-class shares in the next complete issue before attributing a change in headline asking prices to market movement. Check whether collection coverage or the mix of areas has changed. For development or policy decisions, combine this advertised inventory with independently verified planning, pipeline and household evidence.

sales / Price adjustments

Where expectations shift.

Observed advertised price adjustment activity recorded event counts across primary markets rather than discount rates. LAGOS recorded 27 reduction events, followed by ABUJA with 4 recorded reduction events and IBADAN with 2 recorded reduction events.

36 events observed. Peak week: 2026-10-12 (16 events). The data records adjustments to asking prices; it does not establish the final negotiated price.

Reading the evidence

Inventory, property mix and asking-price benchmarks should be considered together. Coverage and class composition can move aggregate figures even when comparable properties have not changed price. See the detailed tables for the observations behind these figures.

03 / rentals · Inventory

Rentals Market Analysis

Rental listings observed via the PS-0 PropertyScraper lens span 9 cities and 201 city/neighbourhood pairs. Lekki Phase 1 (LAGOS) demonstrated the highest volume, averaging 976.8 active listings per observed week. Ikoyi (LAGOS) averaged 560.2 active listings per observed week, while Lekki (LAGOS) recorded an average of 551.2 active listings per observed week.

rentals / Asking prices

Compare asking-price benchmarks.

Advertised asking rent benchmarks reflect class-specific distributions. Within 2 Bed Flats, Tipper Garage (IBADAN) posted a mean observed group median of ₦1.1M/yr (4.0 average weekly listings across 4 priced weeks), while Banana Island (LAGOS) registered ₦30.0M/yr (25.8 average weekly listings). For Terraced Houses, Gwarinpa (ABUJA) stood at ₦6.0M/yr (3.0 average weekly listings), compared to ₦60.0M/yr in Banana Island (LAGOS) with 52.2 average weekly listings.

Where expectations shift.

Price adjustment metrics capture distinct event counts rather than discount rates across observed rental markets. LAGOS recorded 27 reduction events, while ABUJA registered 1 recorded reduction event. EDO recorded 0 reduction events during the observation period.

28 events observed. Peak week: 2026-10-19 (15 events). The data records adjustments to asking prices; it does not establish the final negotiated price.

Reading the evidence

Inventory, property mix and asking-price benchmarks should be considered together. Coverage and class composition can move aggregate figures even when comparable properties have not changed price. See the detailed tables for the observations behind these figures.

Research notes

How to read this report.

Source and scope. PS-0 reconstructs weekly groups from listing records and price-change history. Each group identifies city, neighbourhood, week, property class and market type. The source city field includes city and state-level market labels; location counts do not imply uniform administrative units. Sales and rentals are separate; short lets are excluded. Residential, land and commercial classes may be represented.

Inventory. Peak is the highest weekly total. Cumulative counts measure listing-weeks. The period includes weeks whose start date falls inside its calendar window; a final week can extend beyond month-end. The final week is excluded when its inventory falls below 30% of the preceding weeks' median, a heuristic that may also remove a real decline.

Pricing. Group prices are medians. Area benchmarks average those observed group medians; aggregate prices are unweighted medians of group medians. Affordable and expensive rankings require average observed weekly inventory of at least three and five listings respectively. Amounts are stored in kobo and divided by 100 for NGN display. Rental amounts assume annual asking rents in the source.

Historical limitations. Current listing status, price and property classification are reused in reconstructed weeks. These are not immutable historical price observations. Missing observations and portal access can influence coverage; the pipeline does not explicitly annotate outages.

Days on market. DOM measures first observation to the earlier of last observation and the week's end, with a one-day floor. Discovery can occur after the actual listing date. It is omitted from the main comparisons because this limitation constrains interpretation.

Authorship and use. Research by Isaac Akinmokun, with automated narrative assistance. Figures and tables derive from the computed inputs. This publication supplies general market observations, not investment advice. Source coverage and asking prices should be independently assessed before decisions.

Evidence and reproducibility. The aggregate comparison CSVaggregate comparison CSV (HTML edition) contains every eligible city/area/class group, including observations outside the printed selection. Data definitions and provenanceData definitions and provenance (HTML edition) record the exact source fingerprint, included weeks and selection rules. Inventory eligibility uses observed weeks; city averages use every included report week. A missing area/week is not assumed to be a zero-price observation.

Suggested citation. Akinmokun, Isaac. PS-0 Nigeria Property Market Report: October 2026. Published November 1, 2026. https://reports.akinmokun.com/2026-10/
